open_points.subject: A18 startup cleanup of orphaned value bytes
open_points.text: On start, temporary files, value bytes no record names ... are removed; nothing else is. A spool directory that cannot be removed does not stop the start
open_points.question: What happens when an unreferenced value-byte file cannot be removed: does startup fail, continue while leaving the file unserved, or continue and permit that file to be reused?
options: Continue, leave it unserved, and retry removal at a later start
Continue and allow later equal bytes to reuse it
open_points.default_guess: Refuse startup, because only spool-directory removal is explicitly allowed to fail without stopping startup.

open_points.subject: A18 equal-byte deduplication across startup cleanup
open_points.text: Equal bytes are stored once. On start, ... value bytes no record names ... are removed
open_points.question: Is “Equal bytes are stored once” limited to files concurrently present between startups, or must an orphan removed at startup remain deduplicated across time, despite later equal bytes requiring the file to be published again?
options: Deduplicate only while the published file exists; after startup removal, equal bytes may be published again
Guarantee one publication for a digest across the installation lifetime, so orphan value bytes must not be removed
Treat later publication after cleanup as restoration of the same content-addressed object and explicitly exempt it from the once-only wording
open_points.default_guess: Deduplicate only while the file exists; after startup removes an orphan, later equal bytes are published again.
